decisions.reason: A low-pile carpet close to the core offer costs little to keep in a premium collection, and one year of presence reveals too little to justify abandoning the option.
A hand-knotted wool silk carpet is a high-value showpiece that fits the craftsmanship positioning, and with uncertainty unresolved, keeping the option open is cheap.
This decorative carpet overlaps with other rug options but carries low holding costs, so it is kept until sales evidence resolves its value.
A corner bench builds on the established upholstery and dining offer for residential and hospitality projects, so its option value warrants further time on the market.
A low-pile carpet has minimal keeping costs within a broad portfolio, and no negative signals yet suggest its value will not materialize.
A swivel shell chair line with several models serves both contract and residential markets, and this multi-model investment is worth holding while demand uncertainty resolves.
